answer: Price new identities by the pulse of recent sign-ups: while joins arrive at a normal trickle the entry deposit stays small, but a burst from a farm pushes it up a steep ridge, so the fiftieth clone in an hour pays far more than the first. The deposit comes back after months of honest work, so genuine newcomers lose little. Until then each new account lives on a quiet island with a modest earning cap, so a surge of fakes buys expensive, slow seats rather than a voting bloc.
